name: Dai Wenjian
current_role: Founder of Huochebang (Truck Alliance, merged into Manbang/Full Truck Alliance); reported chairman of Guizhou Aishang Dafeiniu (cattle farming)
profile: Sichuan University finance graduate who was reportedly one of the partners in NVC Lighting (雷士照明) before starting a logistics business in 2005. He built Huochebang, a truck-cargo matching app launched in 2013, which merged with Yunmanman in Nov 2017 to form Manbang (Full Truck Alliance). He later moved into beef cattle farming (Dafeiniu).
interesting_fact: His first attempt at logistics matching - handing about 20,000 satellite navigation units to truckers - failed and lost over 30 million yuan before he pivoted to an app.
deep_cut_fact: Before the app, he ran 13 QQ chat groups of about 500 cargo owners and drivers each across provinces south of the Yangtze, then moved ~60% of those cargo owners onto his own platform.
notes: Sixth Tone romanizes his name as 'Dai Jianwen'. MarketScreener notes he resigned from the Full Truck Alliance board (date not seen). Current role at Dafeiniu sourced only from cnpp.cn profile (https://www.cnpp.cn/focus/231635.html). No published personal contacts found.

name: Yu Weirong
current_role: Shareholder and member of the controlling family of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry (湘佳股份, 002982.SZ); no executive title found
profile: Yu Weirong is the daughter of Yu Ziwen, chairman and co-controller of Xiangjia, a Hunan yellow-feather broiler chicken producer (breeding, slaughtering, chilled poultry, food processing) whose predecessor was founded in 2003 and which listed in Shenzhen in 2020. Her Hurun wealth derives from the family stake in Xiangjia.
interesting_fact: Xiangjia's main revenue comes from chilled poultry meat (about 59% of revenue in H1 2026); the founder started out as a Hunan farmer.
notes: Low public profile; appears in filings only as a shareholder (approx. 3.92m shares per Sept 2026 report) and controlling-family member alongside father Yu Ziwen (source: 2024 pledge notice https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202405151633170502_1.pdf). Best route is via Xiangjia's investor relations / board secretary office.

name: Rong Xiuli
current_role: Chairman, Vanchip (Tianjin) Technology (唯捷创芯, 688153.SH, STAR Market) per 2022 report; founder of Beijing Tianyu Langtong (K-Touch phones)
profile: Engineer turned phone distributor who founded Beijing Tianyu Langtong in 2002 and built the K-Touch (天语) brand, which shipped ~21m handsets in 2008 and made her a Hurun IT-list member. As K-Touch faded in the smartphone era she shifted upstream: Vanchip, founded 2010, designs RF power amplifiers for Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo and Honor and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022.
interesting_fact: Dubbed the 'godmother of shanzhai phones', she built K-Touch by combining MediaTek chips, BYD batteries and Foxconn assembly; in 2019 MediaTek invested in her chip firm Vanchip and dissolved its own PA unit.
deep_cut_fact: She entered Hunan University at 16 to study internal combustion engines and was first assigned to a tractor research institute to develop tractors, earning about 100 yuan a month, before leaving to sell phones.
notes: Chairman title from a 2022 article; not re-confirmed in 2025-26 filings. IR email from Vanchip's 2024 results-briefing notice; board secretary Zhao Yanping handled IR in Dec 2025. Very low media profile.

name: Tao Yishan
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Tangrenshen Group (唐人神, 002567.SZ)
profile: Hunan-born (Ningxiang, b. 1955) agribusiness executive who rose from grain-station worker to director of the Zhuzhou municipal feed factory, then chaired Xiangda Group before becoming chairman of Tangrenshen in 2000. Tangrenshen is a Zhuzhou-based feed, hog-farming and meat-products group listed in Shenzhen; he still chaired its board meetings in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: He was a deputy to China's 10th National People's Congress and has served as executive vice president of the China Feed Industry Association and vice president of the China Meat Association.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1972 at the Hetang district grain station in Zhuzhou, followed by a decade at the Zhuzhou municipal rice mill, before he ran the city feed factory (1985-1993).
notes: Current chairmanship confirmed by Aug 2026 board notice (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202608281828640649_1.pdf). Biographical details come from a user-uploaded profile on maigoo.com; treat as secondary. Route via Tangrenshen board secretary / IR.

name: Tang Xinzheng
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich List 2017-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Yinxin' (real estate). No source found online identifying him or the company beyond the Hurun listing.
notes: Searches for 唐鑫政 with 银信/房地产/胡润 returned no matching person; 'Yinxin' company could not be pinned down. Needs Hurun original listing to identify company and city.

name: Liu Xiaoqing
current_role: Former major shareholder of Dalian Chenxin Network Technology (大连晨鑫网络科技, 002447.SZ)
profile: Most likely the daughter of Liu Dequn, former actual controller of Dalian Chenxin Network Technology (Shenzhen-listed 002447); filings name her as his concerted-action party holding ~7% of the company around 2019-2020. Not the actress of the same name.
notes: The 'Morningstar Network Technology' + shared-with Liu Dequn match points to the Chenxin shareholder (2020 SZSE filing https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-11-04/69822b29-06f3-4e46-acf8-6e376e7f40eb.PDF). The Hurun 1999 appearance may instead be the actress Liu Xiaoqing - possible merged record. Family stake was frozen and transferred/auctioned 2019-2020, so likely no longer UHNW. Not a suitable podcast target.

name: Jing Xiaojun
current_role: Founder, chairman and actual controller, Surfilter Network Technology (任子行, 300311.SZ)
profile: Harbin Institute of Technology PhD who founded Shenzhen-based Surfilter in 2000, a maker of network/data security products, serving as CEO until 2016 and remaining chairman and controlling shareholder. He is also a member of the China Computer Federation. Surfilter forecast a return to profit for 2025 and lifted its risk warning in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: A cybersecurity founder with a doctorate from Harbin Institute of Technology, he has led Surfilter since founding it in May 2000.
deep_cut_fact: In July 2026 he personally donated 3.8 million Surfilter shares (~0.56% of the company) to the Harbin Institute of Technology Education Development Foundation, to fund HIT teaching awards and its Faculty of Computing.
notes: Romanized in English databases as Xiao Jun Jing. Company traded as ST Renzixing; route via Surfilter board secretary/IR.

name: Wang Yongping
profile: Listed on Forbes (2015) and Hurun China (2015-2017) with wealth attributed to 'Xinwei' (telecom). Could not find a source linking 王勇萍 to Xinwei Group (600485.SH) or another Xinwei company.
notes: Xinwei Group's disclosed controlling holders are Wang Jing and concerted parties (Jiang Ning, Liu Yun, Xu Dehuai) per 2018 filing; Wang Yongping not found in searched filings. Identity unresolved.

name: Zhang Kaiyi
current_role: Early executive and shareholder of Sangfor Technologies (深信服, 300454.SZ); Vice President as of 2017 (current title not confirmed)
profile: Long-time Sangfor executive and significant shareholder (about 2.58% per Q1 2020 report) of the Shenzhen cybersecurity and cloud-infrastructure company founded in 2000 by He Zhaoxi (River He) and Xiong Wu. As a VP he was a public spokesman for Sangfor's 2017 push into hyperconverged infrastructure and cloud.
interesting_fact: In a 2017 interview he said Sangfor put 50% of its 2016 R&D budget into hyperconverged infrastructure and cloud products - a big bet for a company then known for security gear.
notes: Not named among Sangfor's actual controllers (He Zhaoxi, Xiong Wu, Feng Yi). Shareholding from 2020 Q1 report (https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-04-25/3ee4f90b-4557-4fc9-ac14-d5bd08a1edc4.PDF). Data-center/cloud angle relevant to podcast.

name: Chi Yanming
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Lanxum / Doushen Education (立思辰 / 豆神教育, 300010.SZ); no company role since Oct 2021
profile: Tsinghua precision-instruments graduate (1990, b. 1966) who founded Beijing Dongfang Office Equipment in 1993, renamed Lanxum (立思辰) in 1999 as an office information-systems outsourcing firm. He steered it into education, renaming it Doushen Education in 2020, then sold down and left; control later passed to Dou Xin after a restructuring.
interesting_fact: His company began as an office equipment seller and outsourced office IT provider before reinventing itself as a K-12 Chinese-language education company.
deep_cut_fact: While still a student at Tsinghua he ran an office equipment agency, Beijing Dangdai Electronics Business Department (北京当代电子经营部), the seed of his later company.
notes: Exited Doushen via share sales/transfers 2019-2024 (reported cash-out ~1.05bn yuan per jiemian/finet summaries); current activities unknown. Low-likelihood podcast target; no published contacts.

name: Ding Xiaoming
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich List 2017-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Green City' (real estate). No source found linking 丁小明 to Greentown China (绿城中国) or another 'Green City' developer.
notes: Greentown China's leadership (Song Weiping, Zhang Yadong, Liu Chengyun, Zhao Hui) does not include Ding Xiaoming; 'Green City' may be a different regional developer. Identity unresolved.

notes: Candidate bio from Lansdowne site (https://www.lansdownepartners.com/?p=682); he gave a 'rare interview' on the Money Maze podcast (https://www.moneymazepodcast.com/podcast/global-investing-public-private-markets-a-rare-interview-with-peter-davies-of-lansdowne-partners). Confirm against the Sunday Times 2020 entry before outreach; common name.

name: Shishir Bajaj
current_role: Former chairman & managing director, Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar (1986-2014); patriarch of the Kushagra Bajaj-led Bajaj Group (sugar, ethanol, power, FMCG incl. Bajaj Consumer Care / Bajaj Corp)
profile: Grandson of freedom fighter Jamnalal Bajaj and younger brother of the late Rahul Bajaj, Shishir Bajaj ran Bajaj Hindusthan, once described as Asia's largest sugar company, from 1986 until handing the chair to son Kushagra in Oct 2014. His branch of the family controls the sugar/ethanol/power group and the FMCG company Bajaj Corp (Bajaj Consumer Care).
interesting_fact: He said his grandfather Jamnalal Bajaj, busy with the Freedom Movement, set up the sugar business (1931, reportedly with Gandhi's blessing) and let Shishir's father run it.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership the family's foundation and Jamnalal Bajaj Trust ran a water programme that deepened 82 rivers and rejuvenated ~120 km of riverbeds around the group's sugar areas; he set a goal of covering 1,000 villages in five years.
notes: Press email is for Neeraj Jha, Group President & Chief Communication Officer (Bajaj Group, Mumbai), as published on the media contacts page. Energy angle: group cogeneration/power business (450 MW per 2014 article). Chairman tenure dates from MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/SHISHIR-KAMALNAYAN-BAJAJ-A040QN/experience/). Current status/alive not verified.

name: Lin Haoliang
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with Lin Ruowen) of Jinfa Labi Maternity & Baby Products (金发拉比, 002762.SZ); chairman 2010-Dec 2025
profile: Shantou entrepreneur (b. 1959) who, with Lin Ruowen, built Jinfa Labi, a Guangdong maker of baby and maternity apparel and products listed in Shenzhen (002762). He chaired the company from Dec 2010 to Dec 2025; a 2025 plan to sell control to Shanghai Yuanyi Chengwu fell through.
interesting_fact: He has served as president of the Guangdong Maternal, Infant & Children's Products Association and as a council member of the Shantou inspection and testing society.
notes: Executive record shows he left the chairmanship on 2025-12-16; current role and controller status after that not confirmed. Stock traded as *ST Jinbi in 2025. Not a natural fit for an energy/data-center podcast.
